multi_key_inception_needs_an_explicit_co.name: multi_key_inception_without_code
multi_key_inception_needs_an_explicit_co.note: with more than one key and no explicit code the prefix branch falls through to `new Prefixer({code: undefined}, sad)`, whose second super() call receives the still-empty identifier field; multisig inception is therefore unreachable through the documented path
multi_key_inception_needs_an_explicit_co.rust_decision: Rust defaults the derivation to Blake3_256 whenever a basic prefix cannot represent the event, so the same inputs produce the event the reference would build with code: E

next_threshold_encoding_follows_the_curr.note: the next-threshold field tests `tholder.num` -- the *current* threshold -- before writing `ntholder.num`, so a weighted current threshold silently forces the next one to text even under integer encoding
next_threshold_encoding_follows_the_curr.rust_decision: reproduced exactly: this changes the bytes the identifier commits to

numeric_current_weighted_next_drops_the_.note: the same condition then writes ntholder.num, which is undefined for a weighted threshold, and JSON.stringify drops the key entirely -- the event has no `nt` field at all and its SAID commits to that malformed shape

next_threshold_validated_against_the_cur.name: valid_next_threshold_rejected
next_threshold_validated_against_the_cur.note: incept compares the next threshold's size against keys.length instead of ndigs.length -- the error message even interpolates ndigs -- so a single-key identifier cannot commit to a 2-of-2 rotation
next_threshold_validated_against_the_cur.rust_decision: Rust validates the next threshold against the next-key digest count
next_threshold_validated_against_the_cur.unsatisfiable_note: the same comparison accepts a 2-of-nothing next threshold, an event committing to a rotation no key set can ever satisfy; Rust rejects it as NextThresholdExceedsDigests

auto_selected_basic_prefix_skips_its_own.note: when the derivation is inferred from a single key the reference *parses* that key instead of deriving from the event, so the non-transferable emptiness checks never run; the result is an identifier that can never rotate yet commits to next keys
auto_selected_basic_prefix_skips_its_own.rust_decision: Rust always derives, so the same checks apply however the derivation was chosen

rotation_cannot_abandon_an_identifier.note: rotate defaults the next threshold to at least one and rejects an explicit zero, so no rotation it builds can ever be the last one; inception has no such restriction
rotation_cannot_abandon_an_identifier.rust_decision: Rust allows an empty next-key commitment in a rotation, as inception already does

rotation_ignores_the_configuration_argum.note: RotateArgs accepts cnfg and never writes it; a caller who sets configuration traits on a rotation silently gets none
rotation_ignores_the_configuration_argum.rust_decision: the rotation builder exposes no configuration setter

rotation_omits_absent_identifier_and_pri.note: both fields are optional and an absent one is simply not written, producing an event with no `i` or no `p` whose SAID commits to that shape
